A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MEGA research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original MEGA benchmark evaluations, deterministic-versus-stochastic analyses, and random-mesh generation results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds masking ablation results in Table 1.

M1.justification: The frozen Mesh-VQ-VAE representation, encoder-decoder architecture, two-stage training, losses, and deterministic and stochastic generation procedures remain unchanged. The additional masking variants are experimental controls, not revisions to the proposed MEGA method.

E1.justification: Both versions use AMASS, MSCOCO, Human3.6M, MPI-INF-3DHP, and MPII, with evaluations on 3DPW, EMDB, and 3DPW-OCC. Unconditional mesh generation and occlusion evaluation already appear in v1; their relocation in v3 does not expand coverage.

E2.justification: v3 adds ScoreHypo to the occlusion comparison and the stochastic HMR comparison, respectively Tables 2 and 3. Existing comparators remain, including VPoser and NRDF in the relocated random-generation experiment.

E3.justification: v3 introduces controls using linear rather than cosine masking and 100% masking during supervised training. Existing benchmark protocols, training epochs, backbones, sample counts, and metrics remain unchanged. Correcting MPJPE's expanded name does not change the metric.

E4.justification: Table 1 adds targeted tests of masking schedules and fully masked supervised training. Conversely, v1's visual PVE–uncertainty comparison is removed, and the error-distribution analysis is reduced from PVE, MPJPE, and PA-MPJPE to MPJPE alone. The average-versus-deterministic analysis and generation-process studies remain.

E5.justification: v3 removes v1's explicit disclosure that experiments were conducted once without testing different seeds. Vertex standard deviations and the discussion of overlapping 95% confidence intervals remain. There is no evidence of added repeated runs or significance testing.

E6.justification: Existing headline MEGA scores and random-generation FID/APD results remain unchanged. New Table 1 entries report linear-masking PVE of 86.5/118.7 mm and full-mask PVE of 81.8/110.3 mm on 3DPW/EMDB; ScoreHypo results are also added. Qualitative examples change, and the PVE–uncertainty finding and two error-distribution panels are removed.

T1.justification: The mathematical tokenization definitions, main masking and generation schedules, and sampling-temperature formulas remain unchanged. The new linear-masking formula specifies an experimental control, without introducing theoretical results, assumptions, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction drop explicit uncertainty-quantification claims and emphasize producing selectable, plausible hypotheses. The central contributions—masked generative HMR, motion-capture pretraining, flexible inference, and state-of-the-art performance—remain. Uncertainty interpretation is still discussed in v3's appendix.

C2.justification: v1 suggests that vertex uncertainty could estimate per-vertex prediction error; v3 drops this link and interprets diversity more cautiously in Appendix D. It adds explanations for the masking ablations and the relevance of excluding 3DPW training data to occlusion evaluation. Extreme-pose and imperfect-ground-truth limitations remain, while the uncertainty-supervision caveat is removed.

D1.justification: v3 identifies the training annotations as pseudo-ground-truth meshes with a CLIFF citation and discloses that the old no-pretraining ablation also used full masking; identical scores do not establish a rerun. Reported training time changes from approximately 3 to 2.5 days, while aggregate nine-day compute disclosure is removed. Detailed optimization settings and the promised release upon acceptance remain.

R1.justification: Related work adds focused citations on motion-capture pretraining, ambiguity, ScoreHypo, and discrete diffusion. It more explicitly distinguishes MEGA's generation paradigm from TokenHMR's regression and VQ-HPS's classification, and contrasts direct 3D masking with earlier pretraining approaches. Publication updates to existing references do not constitute new works.

P1.justification: The experimental narrative and appendices are substantially reorganized: occlusion evaluation and image-conditioned generation-process discussion move into the main text, random generation moves to Appendix C, and diversity interpretation receives Appendix D. The abstract, related work, and conclusion are revised, and supplementary references are consolidated.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a two-column layout, regroups comparison and ablation tables, replaces the opening illustration, and reuses the old opening examples in Appendix Figure 8. Generation-process figures are split and relocated, qualitative galleries are redesigned, and the PVE–uncertainty figure and two distribution panels are removed.

improvement.justification: The added masking controls in Table 1 and ScoreHypo comparisons in Tables 2–3 strengthen support for the existing method. Clearer differentiation from related methods and narrower uncertainty claims also improve the argument. These gains are limited by the removal of the single-run disclosure and some diagnostic evidence; the core method and headline performance remain unchanged.
